paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: a speech can have good words in it and still land on the wrong person. Eliphaz says Job's wickedness is great and his iniquities are endless (Job 22:5). But all we get is Eliphaz's list. God Himself said there is no one on earth like Job (Job 1:8). So when somebody explains your hard season by pointing at your sins, hold up, because that's a guess in a nice suit.

Now the invitation part? That's the good stuff. Eliphaz says, "Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart." (Job 22:22). Coming back to God, listening to Him and keeping His words close is good for any baker on any day, whether the batch came out golden or burnt. Eliphaz even says "the Almighty will be your gold" (Job 22:25), and I'd take that over a cookie jar full of coins any day.

So take the good and test the rest. Eliphaz draws a straight line from Job's pain to Job's sin, and the book already told us Job was blameless (Job 1:8). Be slow to draw that line about a hurting friend, and be gentle when somebody tries to draw it about you. Hang on to your apron, friend, because Job's story is FAR from done.
